column1: # ADR 0082 A2: the glyphs that sofel's interval check reports on Golem's
# test fonts, and the codes Golem root ADR 0390 gives them.
# Columns: font, glyph, sofel kind ("-" for none), Golem codes ("-" for
# none), note. tests/cff_random.rs (sofel-conformance) rebuilds the fonts
# and compares the first three columns.
# The fonts: sans-random and han-random are Golem's
# random-audit/out/*-random.otf, rebuilt from the HarfBuzz test fonts
# SourceSansPro-Regular.otf (glyph 44) and
# SourceHanSans-Regular_subset.otf (glyph 5) with Golem's src/patch.py
# program; the test checks that the bytes are Golem's. The other rows put
# the programs of Golem's review of its ADR 0390 (adr0390-review) and of
# that ADR's boundary table into glyph 44 of Source Sans Pro. n is the
# largest number callsubr takes in Source Sans Pro (the number plus the
# bias is the last entry of its local Subrs INDEX); k in the row names is
# the multiplier of random, as in Golem's boundary table. Every program
# but intcall runs random on its seed path.
# Golem's noto-random.otf is not rebuilt: its source font
# (NotoSerifJP-Regular.otf of a Golem test project) is not in the test
# data. It is CID-keyed with the same program as han-random; run by hand,
# sofel-validate reports no interval diagnostic on it.
# The Golem codes follow the rules of Golem root ADR 0390, which Golem has
# not implemented yet: G08107 a reference outside an INDEX, G08108 a
# reference that cannot be checked, G08109 a glyph FreeType cannot load.
# Golem reports the three independently; sofel reports the first finding
# of a glyph only (ADR 0082), so a glyph with two Golem codes has one
# sofel kind. Golem also gives G08108 to a glyph without random that
# runs more than 100,000 numbers and operators; sofel checks only glyphs
# whose seed path runs random (ADR 0082), so no row has that case.
